collections.title: Early Career Correspondence
collections.description: Responses and introductions connected with Robert Cushman’s early efforts to find theatre-criticism work. These documents are presented as a standalone archival series rather than being attached to any one article.

media.alt: Letter from Anthony Thwaite at the New Statesman to Robert Cushman, dated 6 March 1969
media.caption: Anthony Thwaite, New Statesman — 6 March 1969

items.transcript:
6 March 1969

Dear Mr Cushman,

Thank you for letting me see your drama reviews, but we have Benedict Nightingale as our full-time drama critic (except for occasional pieces from New York, Paris, etc.) and I have no plans to replace him. But we'll make a note of your name.

I enclose your photo-copies.

Yours sincerely,

Anthony Thwaite
Literary Editor
items.transcript_note: Letter text transcribed from the image. Letterhead and recipient address omitted; the signature is rendered as a name.

media.alt: Letter from R. S. Thackeray at The Sunday Telegraph to Robert Cushman, dated 22 March 1969
media.caption: R. S. Thackeray, The Sunday Telegraph — 22 March 1969

items.transcript:
22nd March, 1969.

Dear Mr. Cushman,

I have now read your play notices and I have spoken with the Literary Editor, Anthony Curtis, about your interest in reviewing books. I hope that both he and I will be able to offer you some outlet in the future. As far as theatre notices are concerned an opportunity may come in the holiday season, and I will try to let you know in good time.

Yours sincerely,

R. S. Thackeray
Assistant Editor (Features)

Enc.

collections.title: Farewell to The Observer
collections.date_label: Departure period, with one undated note
collections.description: Notes sent to Robert Cushman around the end of his regular tenure as The Observer’s theatre critic. They are grouped here with the farewell material preserved on The Observer publication page.
